summary: Observation by a motorist of the presence and silent movement of two bright red to orange luminous points; decrease in light intensity and disappearance in the clouds: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Sunday, December 2, 2018, at approximately 7:05 PM, a motorist was intrigued by the presence of two bright red lights in the overcast sky, heading due south. Upon arriving at his destination, the witness found the lights were still visible. He then took two photos and a video with his smartphone. He then saw the two objects gain altitude, following the same trajectory, and disappear into the clouds. No noise was heard during the observation. Only one witness report was collected. The witness likely observed Thai lanterns. The observation is indeed consistent with this: - in appearance: two bright lights of red or orange hue, as described and shown in the video; - in trajectory: the two lights followed each other, which is typical of lanterns traveling in the same direction of the wind. Observations of the movement are very imprecise. We can understand that there is a westward movement (the second UFO, initially further east, is joining the first) and a northward movement (since there is an increase in elevation for the observer looking south), but the magnitudes of these movements are unknown. There is also a significant unknown regarding the wind direction carrying the lanterns; the wind direction measured at ground level varies considerably depending on the nearby weather stations (Istres, Cap-Couronne, Marignane, etc.) and the time around 7 PM. Under these conditions, the compatibility of the observation with the wind cannot be assessed: - in terms of duration and mode of disappearance: the observation duration (10 minutes) is consistent with the lanterns' flight time, and their disappearance is probably caused by the lanterns burning out, which can be gradual and which a witness might mistakenly interpret as the UFOs entering the clouds, whereas the clouds are generally higher than the lanterns' maximum flight altitude. It was a weekend evening, which is conducive to festive events of this type. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation with the naked eye and then with binoculars of a fixed and luminous phenomenon in the night sky: observation of Mars.
description: In the early hours of August 7, 2018, at approximately 1:12 AM, a witness on his outdoor terrace was startled by the sight of a stationary luminous phenomenon in front of him. The witness decided to observe it with binoculars and was astonished to see a luminous circle of different colors with two very bright red and yellow lights at its center. The witness contacted the police and then went to bed at 1:30 AM, still disturbed by the observation. At 5:05 AM, he got up, but the UFO had disappeared. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. This account illustrates the panic that can arise from mistaking a celestial object for another, especially when the witness uses binoculars to observe it. The witness's precise drawings allow us to accurately reconstruct the direction of observation, which was due south. Mars (very bright, magnitude -3.6) is above the mountains, as shown in the drawing. At an altitude of 20 arcseconds, Mars stood out clearly from the mountain peaks, which were no more than 5 arcseconds high as seen by the witness. The witness (typically) overestimated the UFO's altitude (45 arcseconds). Saturn was also visible 30 arcseconds further to the right (west), less bright (magnitude 0) but still brighter than the other stars in the area. This led the witness to believe there were two very bright lights, red (Mars) and yellow (Saturn), surrounded by (normally) white stars. The witness then took binoculars and pointed them at Mars. A witness already misinterpreted a celestial object is often even more so when using binoculars, which are often difficult to focus on (binocular artifacts) or reveal unusual features for someone observing a celestial object through binoculars for the first time. The sky was clear; if the witness had been observing a UFO other than Mars, he would very likely have indicated the presence of Mars, given the accuracy of his drawings. Consequently, GEIPAN concludes in A: observation of Mars.

summary: Observation of the silent North-South passage of a luminous orange object in the night sky: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On July 7, 2018, at approximately 10:45 PM, a witness in his garden saw a glowing orange-red light appear several kilometers above the horizon. As the object silently approached, the witness became increasingly intrigued and considered numerous possible explanations. The object disappeared into a cloud and then reappeared. The observation lasted between one and two minutes. The witness had time to take a picture with his phone before the object vanished "on the spot." No other accounts of this phenomenon have been collected. The witness likely observed a Thai lantern arriving from the north and going out as it passed to his east: - the color ("Orange, very bright, completely illuminated, a bit like the color of glowing embers"); - the shape ("in the distance a ball then a shape... difficult to describe because it was moving, like a molten plasma, rather elongated, somewhat tube-shaped but with a flared rear. The outline was even brighter and very orange, as if on fire"). When the lantern approaches and rises in altitude, the underside of the lantern's burner can obstruct the light, and it is the lantern's outline that appears brighter. The combustion and its flickering give an effect of fire and fluctuating outlines of this fire. Some lanterns may have a flared shape: - the North-South trajectory is consistent with the measured wind, which is from the North (see the website Météociel), - the disappearance is also consistent. The end of combustion can give the impression of "material disappearing on the spot." The fall of the extinguished and dark lantern is not always visible, - a summer weekend night is conducive to a festive event of this type. In this scenario, the lantern passed through a cloud. The witness's perception is indeed that of a fading glow against a cloud background, therefore probably by passing through its lower part. Lanterns rarely fly above 300 m altitude, but the witness mentions the few clouds as Being low in the sky, this description does not contradict the lantern hypothesis. The satellite hypothesis is to be rejected. The shape changes too much in size (as implicitly deduced from the description). Only the ISS could give such an impression of a glow and significant, magnifying size, but the ISS is not in the sky. Moreover, the disappearance cannot occur in this way, in the absence of sustained cloud cover. The meteorite hypothesis is also to be rejected because the duration of the phenomenon is too long (and its angular velocity too slow). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Very bright object moving quickly filmed with a mobile phone: photographic artifact.
description: On May 31, 2018, at 10:00 PM, a teenage girl was intrigued by the intensely yellow color of the stormy sky and filmed it with her cell phone from her balcony. A few minutes later, she told her mother she had filmed "something strange." Her mother provided a statement confirming her observation. No other statements were collected. This is a case of an anomaly created by the camera/video device and therefore not seen by the witness. GEIPAN no longer handles these cases in order to dedicate its resources to phenomena seen in the sky and not those created by devices or elements in the immediate vicinity of the device (e.g., insects, reflections). When we have strong doubts, we send a standard message (see the GEIPAN analysis document), and the witness generally clarifies the situation. We can then either close the case or usefully investigate the phenomenon that was actually seen, and the photo/video is, of course, very helpful. This case has nevertheless been studied and published because it clearly illustrates the difficulty of processing a child's testimony, whether given through interaction with or relayed by their parents. Indeed, this type of testimony is not isolated, and we sometimes struggle to obtain the vigilance or critical thinking of parents following our questions or requests for clarification. We know that a parent is not always best placed to critically analyze their child's statements! In this particular case: - the parent of the minor witness, in response to our standard message regarding the probable strangeness of the photo/video, asserted that their child first saw it with their own eyes and then filmed it. We pointed out the extreme difficulty of detecting such a rapid UFO with the naked eye and starting the video recording, and the parent replied that their child filmed by looking directly at the sky and rotating the device in their hand. - The unusual filming method, the changing description of the observation conditions which contradicts the initial testimony where the child alerted his parents because he FILMED (he didn't say SAW) something strange, all these elements support our doubts about the reality of the visual perception of the strange object; - the parent continued to refute our opinion and maintain that the strange object had been seen, while finding GEIPAN's case classification hasty. We are unable to publish the testimony (the questionnaire and email exchanges beyond GEIPAN's initial standard response) because the parent refused. We conducted a full analysis. We do this when the witness's argument (regarding the truly visual nature of the observation) is strong; here, we did so for illustrative purposes, as explained above. And once again, this confirmed our experience and our need for vigilance regarding anomalies in photos and videos. We took several screenshots of the video (see attached document: 4 moments 922, 2050, 2707). Thanks to the specific IPACO tool, we can show that each time, the strange bright spot is symmetrical (with respect to the center of the image) to the sun. This is indeed a classic optical reflection effect: a very strong light (here, the sun) is duplicated (albeit diminished) by the lens in symmetry with the lens's optical center, the latter being, in principle, coincident with that of the image (or very close, which explains the slight offset). It's important to note that when the viewfinder is in sweep mode, this reflection sweeps twice as fast. We confirm that this is an anomaly perceived without direct visual observation but on a device screen, and that this anomaly results from a photographic artifact. It is possible that the child saw something unusual with their own eyes, but this is certainly not what was reported or what is seen in the video. In conclusion, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: photographic artifact.

summary: Observation by a witness of the passage in the sky of a bright cylindrical ball and a black ball: observation of the passage of an airplane.
description: On May 9, 2018, at approximately 7:30 PM, a witness on a rugby field was intrigued by the passage of a very bright cylindrical sphere and a black sphere across the sky. The black sphere was coming from the northeast and heading southwest. No sound was heard. The observation lasted about a minute before the witness lost sight of the UFO. Nevertheless, the witness had time to take three photographs. No other reports were collected by GEIPAN (the French UFO investigation group). The witness was both excited and troubled by his observation, as he really wanted an explanation (or perhaps a lack of one?). He had, in fact, made other strange observations in the past (without reporting them to GEIPAN), he was well-informed about UFOs, and this time his hopes were high because he had taken photos. He might be disappointed by an explanation that didn't live up to his expectations. Indeed, the speed of movement and the appearance of the UFO in the photo strongly suggest a passenger plane. In the unzipped photo, equivalent to what the naked eye sees, the plane is simply a bright point without a trail (trails not being automatic), a classic aircraft shape. The strangeness for the witness arises from the zoom (or from particularly sharp natural vision) which reveals the elongated, wingless shape. Numerous cases analyzed by GEIPAN show that it is common for only the fuselage to reflect the sun, and the plane thus appears wingless, like a cigar. This is especially true when the sun is transverse to the fuselage and only "sees" the thickness of the wing, as here with a sun at an azimuth of 282° orthogonal to the NE-SW trajectory described for this UFO. And the proof is there, since we find the plane "in question." As the attached reconstruction shows, at 7:29 PM (the time the photo was taken), we have an aircraft flying from NE to SW, and its trajectory as seen from the rugby field matches the witness account. In particular, the photo, thanks to the IPACO software, allows us to determine the UFO's height relative to the tops of the first trees bordering the rugby field to the south. These trees are about 100 meters away, assuming the witness is in the middle of the stands. The treetop height is between 5 and 10 meters, depending on whether the tree is 5 or 15 meters tall (there are two trees of different heights in the photo). This places the UFO at a height in the sky of approximately 35 meters, when we add the heights measured in the photo. And this is indeed the order of magnitude of the aircraft's height, which is shown on the radar capture at 12 km and 10.6 km altitude, or 41 meters above the sky. The difference is explained by unknowns and errors regarding the witness's position along the stands, the knowledge of the tree heights, and the synchronization between the photograph and the aircraft's radar capture. The aircraft was rapidly moving away and descending in altitude. The black UFOs mentioned by the witness are more likely dirt on the lens; in fact, there are many of them. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: aircraft.

summary: Observation of a fixed light with movement effects and color changes: very likely observation of Jupiter.
description: On May 3, 2018, at 10:30 PM, a witness was intrigued by the presence of a fixed light in the low-altitude sky. The witness then described multiple movements (left to right, up and down) and changes in color. No noise was heard. He decided to film his observation, which lasted 3 to 4 minutes. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness most likely observed Jupiter. - There is a good match in the sky's position. Jupiter is indeed in the southeast (123rd) and at a close altitude (9th) to the observed altitude (15th). - The described appearance (a point of light, a fixed light) corresponds well to a star or celestial body. - The color change from white to yellow, "with at times a sort of bursting," corresponds to the effect of the atmosphere, which modifies colors and can create halo effects, particularly in the presence of high humidity. - The perception of slight movement ("the point of light began to move strangely (left to right, up and down, moving away, then towards") results from two classic effects in stargazing: the ocular phenomenon of autokinetic motion (see the article on Reason and Psychology) which creates perceptions of angular movement, and the phenomenon induced by fluctuations in intensity (caused by the atmosphere) which the observer interprets as a radial movement (in their direction) towards or away from the object. - The end of the observation is caused by a passing cloud. Indeed, it is confirmed that the sky was not completely overcast at the end of the day according to data from the Cap-Ferret station (see reconstruction). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: highly probable observation of Jupiter.

summary: Nighttime observations of the silent passage across the sky of a UFO formed by yellow-white "light spikes": observations of Thai lanterns.
description: During an evening with friends in Bourges (18), several people observed at 11:47 PM the silent movement of a UFO (Unidentified Floating Object) in the sky, consisting of several "bright points." The shape first appeared triangular, then circular, but no structure was visible. The object passed over the building and was lost from sight. Only one person in the group reported seeing it. The witnesses most likely observed a display of Thai lanterns: - these were potentially isolated lights because no distinguishing shape connecting them was visible; - these lights were bright and consistent with the appearance of Thai lanterns. - The eastward movement (viewed from northeast to north) is consistent with the original wind direction and measured in Bourges at that time on the website Météociel. - It is a weekend night during the "Printemps de Bourges" festival, a very favorable time for festive events such as lantern releases. Witnesses are surprised by the change in the configuration of the lights, which they may mistake for a change in shape if they imagine a shape between the lights, even though they cannot discern one. Lanterns can fly in close formation and have trajectories that are not perfectly identical due to slight differences in size and wind drag, and small-scale wind variability (especially in urban areas at low altitudes of 100 to 300 meters). Thus, the formation seen from the ground can evolve; in this case, it has changed from something close to a triangle to something close to a circle. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as A: Thai lanterns.

summary: Trace on photograph and intermittent furtive lighting on the ground concomitant with the taking of the photo: observation of an Airbus A321 aircraft.
description: On April 17, 2018, at 9:00 PM, a witness was taking a long-exposure photograph of the sky, directed towards the zenith between Ursa Major and Leo, when he noticed a trail he initially mistook for a simple airplane contrail. At the same time, he realized that the ground in his field of vision was intermittently lighting up for two seconds. Only one witness account of this phenomenon was collected. We demonstrate (see the investigation report) that the witness photographed an Airbus A321 operating the regular Munich-Lisbon route, flight LH1792/DLH05A. Recognition using an online star calibration tool allowed us, firstly, to identify the star field visible in the photograph and through which the aircraft passed. Secondly, superimposing this field with the correctly oriented area of the sky also enabled us to determine the observation azimuth and the axis of the aircraft's trajectory. Finally, cross-referencing this trajectory with those of aircraft passing over the observation area allowed us to definitively identify the aircraft in question. It should be noted, however, that the sequence and synchronization of the white wingtip anti-collision lights on this aircraft are abnormal; Airbus aircraft usually flash twice in very quick succession at a frequency of one hertz, and not four times or randomly as can be seen in the photograph. The overall consistency leads to the conclusion that this is a malfunction of the lights. The strangeness noted by the witness (at the same time, I noticed that in my field of vision the ground was lighting up intermittently for two seconds) is described differently by the witness following a question from GEIPAN, which arose from my astonishment upon seeing the detail in the photograph. It was then that the luminous impression on the ground became conscious of me. The second version is very likely the correct one. The phenomenon (known as amorization) is classic in UFO sightings: an initial strange occurrence creates an understandable state of arousal (which can even lead to panic) in the witness, potentially causing them to associate (and thus amplify) this initial strangeness with other strange occurrences or information that might not have even been perceived (or at least wouldn't have caused concern) in the absence of the initial strangeness. The fleeting nature of this illumination and the lack of direct perception (observation within the field of vision and not along the line of sight) already suggest that it was caused by a local, point-like light source: a passing car shining its headlights in the witness's direction, a neighbor using a flashlight, etc. The additional testimony supports this explanation. The evidence is weak: although a photograph was taken, the original was not provided. The investigator had to reconstruct the angular data using the information provided, given the absence of precise measurements from the witness (angular heights, azimuths, angular distance traveled); - no data exists regarding the witness's environment (precise location, presence of lights, neighbors, roads, etc.) that might have allowed for further investigation of the source of the ground lighting (the false second strangeness); - it should also be noted that the witness described the second strangeness in the initial testimony in a different (and indeed stranger) way than the actual awareness he later claimed to have had of it during the observation. This lack of consistency, however, does not preclude the explanation, as it is so compelling given the other available elements. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: Observation of an Airbus A321 aircraft, flight LH1792/DLH05A en route to Lisbon. Strangeness perceived a posteriori upon viewing the photo.

summary: Long observation of a circular shape of intense white color with filaments; fixed object in the night sky: observation of Venus.
description: On Wednesday, April 4, 2018, at 9:00 PM, a witness was intrigued by the presence of a very bright and stationary UFO in the night sky. The witness described a flashing, circular object with what appeared to be long filaments. He observed the phenomenon for 40 minutes and recorded a video. The object then disappeared and was obscured by a cloud. Three members of his family witnessed the event, but only one testimony was recorded. This testimony was clearly an observation of Venus. The witness himself referred to Venus. The intensity seemed stronger to him, and he could make out filaments around it. It was verified that in the direction of the reported observation, "towards the Montchat district," at approximately 280°/290° azimuth, Venus was indeed located around 280° and at an altitude of approximately 10° (the witness indicated 10° to 15°). This proximity is beyond doubt. If the UFO were not Venus, it would have been noticed by the witness near the UFO at some point during this long observation, as the clouds in the direction of the UFO are transient (as shown in the account and the photo). It is common for intensive observation of Venus to produce impressions of beams, in this case, filaments. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: Venus.

summary: Observation of a luminous sphere of varied colours with a slow descending trajectory: observation of Venus.
description: On March 31, 2018, between 9:30 PM and 9:41 PM, a witness on their balcony was intrigued by a bright, multicolored sphere of light. The UFO followed a downward trajectory and slowly disappeared behind the hill of Notre Dame de la Garde. Only one eyewitness account was recorded. The witness saw Venus. They used the following expression: "The most descriptive analogy is as if a star were slowly falling from the sky, in slow motion." Indeed, Venus, low on the horizon, "fell from the sky in slow motion," because during the observation (10 minutes), Venus moved from 2nd to 0.5th azimuth. It's slow, but when observed close to the horizon, the movement is clearly perceptible. Venus (283rd azimuth) was slightly to the left of Notre Dame de la Garde (290th) and to the right of Rigel (237th), like the UFO described by the witness. But the witness ruled out Venus because he was convinced that Venus was hidden by the hill of Notre Dame de la Garde. And he was wrong. The attached reconstruction shows that in the direction of Venus's observation, the highest obstacle is about 60m higher than the base of the witness's building, or about 50m higher than the witness on the 4th floor. Located at 3900m, this point corresponds to an elevation of 0.7e, and therefore Venus at 2e is visible, and it is normal that after 10 minutes it would have passed below the horizon (0.5e for an obstacle at 0.7e). The appearance of the UFO is perfectly consistent with Venus low on the horizon, with changing colors due to atmospheric effects. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies case A: Venus.

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of an elongated and white object in the sky: observation of the passage of an airplane.
description: On Saturday, March 31, 2018, at 7:37 PM, a witness at his window observed a long, white object moving across the clear sky. It moved quickly in a straight line towards the southeast. The witness filmed the scene and then, after 50 seconds, returned to his activities. Only one witness statement was collected along with the video. The witness observed an airplane. The video shows the unidentified flying object (UFO) passing transversely to the point of view from the house, which faces southeast. Indeed (see reconstruction), an airplane is seen passing at that moment, flying from southwest to northeast, and therefore parallel to the horizon, as indicated by the witness, at an elevation of approximately 45 degrees, consistent with the appearance of the video. The witness does not recognize the airplane, even though there is an airplane sound in the video. He is puzzled by: - the lower altitude than an airplane. Indeed, it is at an altitude of 9000m, lower than a cruising flight; - the shape, indeed, it looks like a cigar. This is typical. When the sun is very low and illuminates the aircraft with a strong transverse beam (sun due east), the fuselage reflects strongly, and the only visible wing is illuminated according to its cross-section, and therefore with little or no reflection; - the absence of a contrail; contrails are far from systematic and depend on atmospheric conditions and/or altitude. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: aircraft.

summary: Observations by two witnesses of the silent movement in the night sky of 7 reddish luminous phenomena: probable observations of Thai lanterns.
description: On Friday, March 30, 2018, around 10:00 PM, a witness (T1) left his house and saw a reddish light moving across the sky and disappearing. He then saw two other luminous phenomena of the same type and took a photograph with his cell phone. One of the two lights began to turn towards the witness as he returned home. He went back outside accompanied by his partner (T2), and together they observed up to seven luminous phenomena moving silently across the night sky. Only these two testimonies were recorded. One of the witnesses disputes the initial explanation from GEIPAN (the French National Center for Experimentation on Astronomy), yet the observation is likely related to the movement of Thai lanterns: the color, the procession of several UFOs (Unidentified Floating Objects) one after the other, the occurrence on a weekend night, and the movement in the direction of the wind (from SE to NW, see attached file) all support this hypothesis. T1's main objection is that at one point a UFO (Unidentified Flying Object) turned in its direction before resuming its normal course. This doesn't contradict the hypothesis because: - it could be a misinterpretation. UFOs move at mid-altitude in the sky, far from vertical. If the lantern shines brighter at a certain point, it's common for this to be interpreted as the UFO approaching the witness horizontally. Similarly, a decrease in intensity would have been perceived as moving away; - it's entirely possible that a generally well-oriented wind is locally accompanied by disturbances (woods, urban development, rivers) and follows a non-straight path. A lantern separated from the others, or all the lanterns in a line, could follow this wind pattern. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable sightings of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation and photography from a cruise ship of an extremely bright white phenomenon in the night sky: observation of Jupiter.
description: On Friday, March 2, 2018, at 2:32 AM, a witness was on the balcony of a cruise ship cabin in the Mediterranean. The sky was illuminated by a full moon and dotted with clouds. While attempting to take souvenir photos of the moonlight, the witness was surprised and intrigued by an extremely bright, white phenomenon. The witness took two photographs just before the UFO suddenly disappeared. Upon returning to their cabin, the witness was surprised to have been outside in the cold much longer than they had anticipated. Only one witness statement was collected. The witness observed and photographed Jupiter. The UFO depicted in the photo is located precisely at Jupiter's position: - this UFO is situated slightly less than 90 degrees to the left of the Moon, since the Moon is shown directly to port of the ship and the UFO is shown almost directly aft (slightly to port as seen in the photo) of the ship. The witness's drawing also shows this nearly 90° difference between the Moon and the UFO; - thanks to the analysis software IPACO, it is easy to determine the UFO's altitude above the horizon and also to measure that of the Moon. The latter allows us to find the exact time of the photo; - we verify that at the time and location of the observation, Jupiter, like the UFO, was at an altitude of 19° above the horizon and offset by 85° to the left of the Moon. Due to a long exposure time (1 second), Jupiter appears with significant movement, creating variable arabesques from one image to the next. The photo largely contributed to the strangeness perceived by the witness, far exceeding what he could have seen with his own eyes. For example, he considers that the two successive photos correspond to different faces of the evolving UFO (he says, "which is very clearly determined by the second photo taken 4 seconds later, which shows another very different face"). The witness speaks of a "clear sky with a few remnants of clouds from time to time," which perfectly explains why his gaze was drawn to Jupiter, a very bright celestial body that evening, as well as the sudden disappearance of the UFO by a cloud that obscured Jupiter. This testimony illustrates what happens to many witnesses, regardless of their background: - the level of strangeness that a star can generate, and in particular here the component of strangeness created by the camera: this witness loses his sense of time (1 hour 40 minutes actually occupied by the UFO versus 15 minutes perceived), perceiving "an immense flying object, extremely bright and of a very surprising shape, appearing to be larger than a large airplane"; - The satisfaction a witness can derive from the sensation and the luck of having seen and photographed a UFO; - The need, when faced with a genuinely observed strangeness, to find an explanation for being the only one to witness it, while others were in a position to do so. Here, our witness believes that the ship's crew "most likely decided not to publicize the information, despite their interest in this undoubtedly TOO strange phenomenon, for fear of unsettling some passengers or crew, especially since it was a cruise." GEIPAN classifies the case as A: Jupiter sighting.

summary: Observation by a motorist of the movements and stops of a luminous white ball in the clear sky and star: observation of Jupiter and illusion of the "following ball".
description: On February 25, 2018, at 3:30 a.m., a motorist observed a bright white ball in the clear, star-like sky. This ball appeared to move and stopped when the motorist stopped their vehicle. No sound was heard. The passenger filmed the phenomenon. Only one witness statement was collected. This case is a prime example of the "following ball" illusion that can be caused by mistaking a celestial body for another when the witness is in motion. Here, we have a video of the witness during the act of moving. The witness's initial confusion stemmed from not recognizing the celestial body's appearance. When the witness's car maintained a relatively constant course, the celestial body appeared stationary relative to the vehicle and moved across the landscape. Since the witness did not see the celestial body but a UFO (Unidentified Flying Object) and perceived it to be at a close distance, this movement along the landscape was perceived as the UFO moving parallel to the vehicle, mimicking its stop-and-go motion. When the witness's heading changed, the UFO's position relative to the road changed. The video clearly illustrates these anomalies perceived by the witness. The attached reconstruction unequivocally shows that it was a very bright Jupiter that evening, reconstructed at two points along the route, once with Jupiter aligned with the road, and another time to the left. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: Jupiter sighting.

summary: Observation above the rooftops of a UFO composed of a juxtaposition of green lights arranged in a rosette and a mobile green beam of light in the overcast night sky: probable observation of a drone for recreational use.
description: On January 28, 2018, at 2:45 a.m., the witness got up to care for her sick husband. Her attention was drawn to a very intense glow seen almost due north through the living room window. The witness saw a series of green lights arranged in a rosette and a green beam of light moving in all directions, sweeping around the area. The unidentified flying object (UFO) turned on and off completely and moved several times. No noise was heard during the UFO's movements, but the witness never opened the living room window. The UFO then moved toward the witness, who, frightened, crouched against the living room wall. When the witness looked out the window again, the UFO had disappeared. The observation lasted between 30 and 45 seconds. No other witness statements were collected. The description conveyed a phenomenon previously unknown to GEIPAN (see the investigation report). A plausible hypothesis has been established based on the appearance and behavior of the UFO: the use of a drone equipped with LEDs and a laser beam. Examples on the internet show recreational drones (online at this address) with a laser beam evolving at night, exhibiting characteristics that closely match the observation: - the beam's movement in all directions, - its green color, - the beam's thickness; the witness's observation of a 30 cm thickness corresponds to a laser beam, while the observation of small particles within this beam is characteristic of a light diffraction phenomenon in the presence of aerosols or fine microscopic particles. These examples of recreational drones do not exhibit a green light rosette surrounding the green beam. However, adding green LEDs (the modular possibilities are numerous) to various ends of the drone can certainly create such an effect. Angular and distance estimates made using testimony and photographs taken during the cognitive interview suggest a sufficiently large drone (1 m) such as those used professionally or even militarily. The presence of this drone in a residential area at 2 a.m. is understandable for recreational use, given that such activity is prohibited and must involve as few witnesses as possible, and that the desired sensation is stronger in an area where the beam can interact with obstacles and facades. It is much less understandable for a drone intended for professional or military use. One might question the reason for such a swirling beam in one case and the hypothesis of specific training exercises in the other, which clashes with the fact that the authorities at the nearby training camp (Frileuse camp in Beynes) indicated no operations of any kind that night. The presence of a recreational drone is more likely, while the angular size suggests a professional drone. However, an overestimation of size (by a factor of 2) by the witness cannot be ruled out despite the reliability of the reference points used (space between two trees), just as it is possible that a professional-grade drone could have been used for recreational purposes. The consistency of the testimony is very good, both in terms of information and reliability. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of a drone for recreational use.

summary: Observation of a round, brown object in a photograph: probable error in interpreting a photograph or video.
description: On January 21, 2018, at 11:55 AM, a passenger in a moving car took two photos, one after the other. He observed that in the first photo, a round, brown object appeared in the sky. Nothing appeared in the second photograph. Only one witness statement was collected. The evidence suggests that the witness most likely did not see the UFO with his own eyes, only through the lens of his camera. Indeed, to the question, "Did other witnesses see the same phenomenon as you? If so, how many?", the witness replied, "Only myself, through my camera lens." Under these circumstances, the most likely explanation, based on GEIPAN's experience, is that it's a camera artifact, in this case probably a nearby insect or bird that he couldn't capture but which wouldn't escape a digital camera even at 1/400th of a second. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable error in interpreting a photograph or video. For several years now, GEIPAN has no longer processed testimonies that don't demonstrate that the strange phenomenon was observed with the naked eye, without an optical instrument. Traces from optical instruments are only considered when they are additional.

summary: Observations by two witnesses of the evolution in the sky of a rounded shape of orange colour; no noise heard: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On Thursday, January 18, 2018, at 6:27 PM, two witnesses were intrigued by the movement of a round, intensely orange, glowing shape in the sky, which suddenly changed direction. No noise was heard during the observations. Observer T1 took a photograph. The round shape, the bright orange color, and the predominantly west-to-east movement consistent with the recorded wind (see the Infoclimat website) all suggest that the flight of a Thai lantern is a highly probable hypothesis. Lanterns are usually released on weekends, but a festive event (such as a birthday) can also take place on a Thursday evening. It should be noted that the weather was rainy but had cleared an hour earlier. The movement observed by T1 between due west at 50° elevation and east at 30° elevation corresponds to a displacement of the UFO of 250 to 500 meters, depending on whether its flight altitude was 100 to 200 meters (a typical case for a Thai lantern). These displacement values are consistent with a measured wind speed of approximately 20 km/h and a reported observation duration of around one minute. Witness T1 reports an uneven glow with additional glows above and below. This indicates that he saw the UFO quite close. Indeed, he describes it as having the angular size of an airplane, even though it was 12 km from an airport. A lantern seen at 100 meters has an angular size equivalent to that of the Moon and exhibits uneven colors; its color can vary depending on the angle of observation. Witness T2, for his part, only notes a bright orange. The photograph does not provide any further information. Witnesses describe a straight trajectory followed by a turn, the extent and direction of which are difficult to assess. T1 is best positioned to observe it, as it appears the UFO passed close to the vertical; the heading changed from SE to E. For T2, the impression seems to be of a southward turn. In any case, they are located near a river, a situation conducive to local wind shifts or gusts. GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of a Thai Lantern.
